one_line: A correctness-gated browser WebGPU experiment and verification lab with shared agent/UI state.
what_it_does: Runs local proof-of-work/WebGPU experiments, compares outputs against references, and exposes guided/advanced verification controls to agents and humans.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools plausibly improve repeatability and correctness gating for technical experiments, though a capable agent could drive much of the visible dashboard with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes correctness-gated experiments and shared human/agent state.
About text names CPU reference verification, test vectors, profiling, and workgroup experiments.
Frame sheets show a rendered verification dashboard, but no legible tool trace.
execution_rationale: A coherent, technically focused dashboard is visibly implemented, but evidence is repetitive and mostly idle/low-resolution; end-to-end GPU execution is not clearly proven.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show populated WebGPU/proof-of-work UI and status cards.
Devpost screenshot shows a consistent dashboard with Ready state and explicit safety messaging.
Screenshot also shows GPU hashing inactive and compute status not implemented.
impact_rationale: Useful for developers and learners inspecting browser compute and verification, but the audience and practical outcome are niche and the evidence of delivered results is limited.
impact_evidence: About text frames it as a local research and crypto-onboarding/inspection tool.
No mining, wallet, payout, or blockchain dependency keeps the use case safely scoped.
creativity_rationale: Combines browser GPU experimentation with explicit refusal of unsupported performance conclusions and agent-operable verification.
creativity_evidence: Correctness-gated GPU lab and safety boundary are a fresh synthesis.
Shared human/agent experiment state is pursued beyond a generic chat panel.
usability_note: Organized technical dashboard, but dense/repeated evidence and unclear active workflow reduce confidence in usability.
red_flags: Frame sheets do not clearly show WebMCP invocation or a completed GPU run.
Devpost screenshot visibly reports CPU mode and an unimplemented compute status.
standouts: Explicit safety/no-live-mining boundaries.
Verification-oriented product framing rather than superficial tool exposure.
advance_reason: Credible focused implementation and meaningful WebMCP angle, though technical execution merits further verification.

one_line: A conditional form that teaches agents its current schema, rejects invalid answers, and gates proposals through human approval.
what_it_does: Models a work-authorization form whose applicable questions and tools change with answers; validates inputs, queues agent proposals, and reserves attestation/signature for the human.
leverage_rationale: The page-local conditional schema and shared answers make WebMCP central: a detached backend or UI-driving agent would lack the exact live rules and state.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates one tool changing from one field to four based on current category/state.
Transcript shows malformed input rejected with exact rule/example, then corrected.
Human approval queue and suspended signature call are explicit shared-state boundaries.
execution_rationale: The transcript demonstrates a coherent multi-step workflow with dynamic tools, validation, correction, approval, and human-only signing; visual sheets support the integrated form/tool inspector, though persistence is not shown.
execution_evidence: 170-second transcript covers category selection, schema changes, validation, correction, approvals, filing checks, and signature boundary.
Frame sheets show the form alongside a dark tool panel with changing tool/output states.
Devpost packaging visibly lists many conditional form tools.
impact_rationale: Targets a real, high-stakes audience struggling with long conditional government forms and reduces both agent error and unsafe autonomous attestation.
impact_evidence: About text explains eligibility categories rewriting roughly forty questions.
Human must approve every proposed value and cannot delegate certification/legal consent.
creativity_rationale: The interaction model—page authority dynamically teaching the agent, refusing invalid moves, and suspending human-only commitments—is unusually original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Dynamic registration of applicable tools is central to the concept.
Correction loop and deliberate signature/certification boundary are memorable design choices.
usability_note: The guided form and explicit correction/approval flow appear usable, though the contact sheets are too small to assess details.
red_flags: No independent evidence of backend persistence or production legal/compliance readiness.
standouts: Strongest packet-level proof of WebMCP changing the interaction model.
Excellent human-authority boundaries for sensitive form completion.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, clear real-world value, and unusually complete demonstrated workflow.

one_line: An evidence-first decision room where agents structure sourced research while humans retain final authority.
what_it_does: Maintains candidates, constraints, evidence records, conflicts, missing fields, proposals, and persisted audit history in a shared decision workspace.
leverage_rationale: Agents need the exact live room state and can add structured candidates/evidence while human edits remain visible; UI-driving automation is materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly describes read/add/attach/conflict/proposal tools over the same live room.
No finalize_decision agent tool; final action is human-only.
Frame sheets claim 16 native tools, 5/5 smoke checks, and three candidates added through WebMCP calls.
execution_rationale: Strongly coherent evidence-first presentation with visible discovery/smoke-test and shared-state outcomes, but screenshots repeat and do not expose detailed traces.
execution_evidence: Frames show Native WebMCP verified, 16 tools discovered, 5/5 smoke test, and shared live state.
Another frame claims persisted auditable change history.
Devpost preview shows evidence health metrics with conflict and missing fields.
impact_rationale: Research and technology decisions have a clear need for provenance, conflict visibility, and human approval; the product directly addresses that workflow.
impact_evidence: About text identifies fragmented transcripts/spreadsheets/tabs and overconfident agents as the problem.
Visible metrics surface evidence records, conflicts, and missing fields.
creativity_rationale: A durable decision room that treats uncertainty, provenance, and human finalization as product primitives is a fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Evidence health and auditable collaboration are integrated into the core workflow.
Deliberate absence of agent finalization reinforces the concept.
usability_note: Clean evidence/status presentation; detailed interaction quality is not inspectable from the repeated sheets.
red_flags: Tool names, schemas, and persistence/reload proof are not visible.
standouts: Quantified native-tool smoke test.
Shared-state mutation plus human-only final decision.
advance_reason: A strong, differentiated research workflow with credible visible WebMCP state changes.

one_line: A React SDK that keeps agent connection, live actions, history, and permissions visible inside the app.
what_it_does: Adds an in-frame camera-rig UI around agent work, including deep-link onboarding, connection status, work states, history, and permission prompts.
leverage_rationale: Visibility and permission UX materially improve agent collaboration, but the underlying app actions could generally be performed by ordinary automation.

Frames show an explicit WebMCP Tools panel and interaction area.
Frames are repetitive and tool text is illegible.

impact_evidence: About text identifies invisible calls and lack of feedback as the problem.
React SDK framing suggests reuse across projects.
creativity_rationale: The camera-rig metaphor and multiplayer framing offer an original interaction model for agent UX beyond chat.
creativity_evidence: Keep the Agent Action in Frame is a distinctive product thesis.
Connection/live work/history/permission are treated as first-class UI.
usability_note: Strong visual storytelling and likely helpful visibility layer; actual onboarding and permission interaction are not fully evidenced.
red_flags: No clear live action result, permission event, or multi-user synchronization proof.
standouts: Distinctive agent-in-frame/multiplayer UX concept.
SDK framing broadens usefulness beyond a single app.
advance_reason: Original agent-infrastructure concept with strong packaging; advance for its UX thesis despite thin execution proof.

one_line: A public systemd crash bench where humans and agents generate safe remediation files from pasted status output.
what_it_does: Parses systemd status or journal snippets and proposes restart drop-ins, watchdog timers, rollback, and hardening plans without touching a host.
leverage_rationale: Page-native structured generators let agents reliably produce typed remediation artifacts against the same workspace, safer than generic UI scraping or freeform advice.
leverage_evidence: About text lists six concrete registered tools and shared workspace behavior.
Human and agent use the same authoritative generators.
Strictly read-only with respect to real hosts; no SSH/install/email.
execution_rationale: Scope is coherent and safety boundaries are explicit, but the packet has no frame sheet or video and the screenshot alone cannot prove generators execute.
execution_evidence: About text gives a specific prompt and complete tool list.
Devpost screenshot provides packaging evidence but not a run result.
Demo is reported alive, supporting plausibility but not end-to-end proof.
impact_rationale: Targets operators who routinely paste systemd failures into chat and offers concrete, reviewable remediation artifacts with no host-side risk.
impact_evidence: Problem and target operator workflow are explicitly described.
Generated outputs include restart, watchdog, rollback, and hardening plans.
creativity_rationale: A focused read-only operations workbench with shared page-native generators is a useful, safety-conscious WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Same generator functions serve human UI and agent tools.
Read-only bench avoids the common dangerous automation pattern.
usability_note: Narrow workflow and clear outputs should be approachable, but visible execution is not demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted frame sheets/video; screenshot is packaging only.
No actual generated artifact visible in packet evidence.
standouts: Excellent safety boundary: proposes files without host access.
Concrete operator-oriented tool surface.
advance_reason: Strong practical fit and safety design, but deserves execution verification because visual evidence is thin.

one_line: Turns an exact wall-art request into a validated, printer-packed fabrication package through structured tools.
what_it_does: Creates deterministic wall art, applies printer-bed constraints, inspects geometry/packing, and prepares an export for human download.
leverage_rationale: The agent can translate natural-language dimensions/aesthetic intent into deterministic geometry, enforce fabrication constraints, inspect exact counts, and prepare a deliverable in one shared state—far more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text names four focused tools spanning create, constrain, inspect, and prepare.
Specific result: 81 parts across 62 plates at exact 48x48 inches.
Final download remains a visible human action.
execution_rationale: The packet gives unusually concrete deterministic counts, measurements, package size, and visible multi-state frame evidence, though no video trace.
execution_evidence: About text reports exact dimensions, 81 parts, 62 plates, and 656,651-byte package.
Frame sheets show the visible fabrication workflow/editor across states.
Human-controlled final download is a coherent completion boundary.
impact_rationale: Directly serves makers who want custom statement art that is actually manufacturable on their printer, connecting creative intent to a deliverable.
impact_evidence: Concrete four-foot-square fabrication request and fixed palette.
Inspection confirms parts fit printer plates.
creativity_rationale: The concept meaningfully combines generative art direction, deterministic geometry, constraint solving, inspection, and fabrication packaging in an agent-native flow.
creativity_evidence: Moves beyond image generation to physically printable, inspected output.
Shared editable project and validation-before-export are deeply integrated.
usability_note: Judge Quick Start and visible staged workflow suggest a clear path from request to export.
red_flags: No readable direct invocation trace; exact claims rely on submission text and screenshots.
standouts: Excellent WebMCP fit for precise multi-step fabrication.
Human-controlled download and validation snapshot are strong safety/product boundaries.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets: transformative structured leverage, concrete output evidence, and memorable creative ambition.

one_line: A searchable spatial scene index that lets agents understand places, route around changes, and assess capture quality.
what_it_does: Models a transit station with entities, regions, relationships, accessibility routes, reversible lift closures, weak-evidence detection, and recapture recommendations.
leverage_rationale: The agent needs live camera, selection, overlays, route, and staged scenario state; narrow page-native tools make spatial reasoning/action substantially more reliable than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About text names tools for search, camera movement, accessible routing, scenario changes, evidence quality, recapture, and undo.
Route changes after closing Lift 1 and reports corridor readiness.
Synthetic deterministic splat fixture is candidly identified and supports complete reproducible behavior.
execution_rationale: The described judged path is complete and stateful, with reversible changes and visible 3D consequences; image evidence was not fully available due transient rate limits, so confidence is reduced.
execution_evidence: About text specifies entrance-to-platform route, lift closure, alternate route, weak capture evidence, and undo.
Packet reports a live demo and a deterministic fixture.
Referenced frame sheets were submitted but vision inspection hit a transient rate limit.
impact_rationale: Accessible wayfinding in complex places is a high-value problem for travelers and disabled users; route alternatives and evidence quality directly address trust and safety.
impact_evidence: Use case explicitly concerns accessible gates, lifts, obstacles, and route constraints.
Reports capture-quality/readiness weakness rather than overstating synthetic data.
creativity_rationale: Combining Gaussian-splat spatial understanding, accessibility routing, reversible what-if scenarios, and capture-quality reasoning is highly novel and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Scenario state changes the route and exposes alternate paths.
Evidence-quality and recapture-position recommendations extend beyond ordinary 3D viewing.
usability_note: Judged path is clearly specified, but 3D interaction usability cannot be verified from the unavailable image analyses.
red_flags: Frame-sheet visual review was blocked by transient vision rate limits.
Synthetic fixture means real-world capture performance is not demonstrated.
standouts: Exceptional spatial/WebMCP interaction model.
Honest synthetic-fixture disclosure and reversible accessibility scenarios.
advance_reason: Highly ambitious, high-impact spatial accessibility concept with unusually strong WebMCP indispensability; advance with visual verification follow-up.
